features.title: Subagent model routes follow the saved setting in running threads
features.summary: The forked subagent and subagent_fork tools keep upstream's schema and delegation behaviour, but the allowed child model routes are re-read from the Subagents model-selection setting at each delegation or list_subagent_models call. A changed list appends a replacement subagent/model-selection-policy event, and the policy projection keeps the latest one, so a route added after a thread started is accepted without a new thread.
failureModes: A profile whose preset-standard delegation rows still name @deepseek-ai/dsh-tool-subagent keeps the frozen per-Session route list.
A thread that started with model selection off keeps a tool without provider/model fields until a new thread; turning the setting off mid-thread keeps the last recorded routes.

features.title: subagent starts a child as a configured agent
features.summary: The forked subagent tool declares an optional agent argument (a handle; constant schema, also without a provider). An agent registry providing @dshfiles/tool-subagent/agent-resolver decides the agent (argument, else the caller's default) or refuses it. The child gets the agent's route (explicit provider/model win and stay under the Session policy; the agent's own route is admitted because the user configured it), its preset (explicit agent_preset wins) and a bounded preamble before the task; the tool reserves the child's Session id and records its agent before starting it, so the child's first request has that agent's tools. subagent_fork takes no agent. list_subagent_models without arguments also lists the agents the caller may start.
failureModes: Without @dshfiles/agents loaded, agent is refused with the plugin to enable; omitting it keeps upstream behavior.
A backend outside the Host (no reserved child ids) refuses agent, since the agent's tools could not apply to it.

features.title: Keep a delegated child working when its turn hands the task back
features.summary: A delegated child that ends a turn as completed while its closing text hands the task back (reassign, cannot complete, no implementation, unfinished, remains unverified, do not land, not implemented, hand back, take over) receives one continuing message at the loop's turn-stopping boundary, so the same turn runs another step instead of the parent receiving a hand-back as the child's result. The wording decides, not the tool count: a turn that fetched, rebased and installed and then handed back is resumed too. A turn that already changed files (fileChangeTools) or ran jj describe/jj commit is real work and is never resumed, and minToolCalls only resumes a turn that quit with no closing text. The guard is bounded per child: after maxResumes messages it reports the completion normally and notes the hand-back to the parent.

configuration.constraints: Boolean; false is the off switch.
Non-negative integer; resumes a turn that quit with no closing text and fewer calls than this. A hand-back is resumed whatever the count; 0 drops the silent-quit trigger.
Non-negative integer; continuing messages one child may receive before the parent is told.

configuration.defaultValue: reassign, cannot complete, no implementation, unfinished, remains unverified, do not land, not implemented, hand back, handoff, take over
configuration.constraints: Case-insensitive regular expression sources; an invalid source is reported and skipped.
Non-empty array of tool names, matched without their namespace; a turn with any of these calls is work, so its hand-back wording is never resumed.

configuration.defaultValue: You stopped without implementing. Continue: implement the next step of your task; only stop on a real blocker, and name it.
configuration.constraints: Non-empty text of the one continuing message.

failureModes: A child spawned under a preset without this package has no guard; its hand-back stays a completed result.
Only a completed stop boundary is inspected: an errored or aborted child turn already reports itself.
A file-changing tool outside childTurnGuard.fileChangeTools is not recognized, so such a turn's hand-back costs up to maxResumes extra steps.
A real blocker reported as a hand-back costs up to maxResumes extra steps before the parent sees it.
